audience.role: Plugin users, 0.6.1 upgraders, and maintainers evaluating dependency risk and acceptance scope

checks.note: README explains use and operation; changelogs record deltas; release draft frames the upgrade; security and acceptance record detail risks and scoped evidence.
Each README gives prerequisites, candidate or published installation path, composer command, report paths and deterministic option; upgrade and risk decisions are stated.
First-use action and outcome are concrete in each README. Dense internal terms occur chiefly in advanced or maintainer sections; the manual CLI invocation warrants clarification.
Candidate and pending publication, the dependency decision, exact-commit CI, host/platform boundaries and historical artifact reuse are distinguished in the documents.
The three first paths lead from purpose and result to prerequisites, security and installation; the first command at line 51 follows material risk and publication caveats.
English, Chinese and Russian README first-use paths are independently understandable; Russian screenshot and change history are English-only, as noted in findings.

findings.message: The manual semantic examples use bare dsh-session-insights after the managed installation introduced an absolute $CLI path; unless PATH is configured separately, readers may be unable to run them. The Chinese and Russian editions repeat this at line 187.

The Russian README uses the English dashboard screenshot and links to the English changelog (line 3); Russian readers can follow first use, but visual and release-history language coverage is incomplete.

The default model-assisted command queues serial batches, but does not set a reader expectation for waiting or say that elapsed time varies. The Chinese and Russian first-use paths make the same omission.

limitations: Cold reading and structural audit only; factual correctness, operational commands, native platform acceptance, model output, UI behavior and publication were not independently verified.

Schema permits only readme, changelog and release_notes roles: SECURITY.md and the acceptance record are classified as release_notes solely to include and bind their bytes; their actual roles are security policy and candidate evidence.
Russian README is maintained, but a Russian changelog and Russian release-note block are not present in the reviewed set.
No external network, UI, model requests, implementation history, private reports, prior receipt or claim ledger was consulted.
